comment: The thing you're graded most on is exams. Exams are like a total of 65%, then lab is the second biggest at 15%, then homework and quizzes at 10%. You have quizzes about every week. The exams are a lot harder than the quizzes and homework. However, I thought the final exam was at least slightly easier than the other exams.
Don't take him. Almost all of the grade is based on tests.
Definitely take physics with Hodge! He is so organized, explains concepts very well, and all quizzes/tests mimic hw, so you feel prepared. He also loves physics and is fun to listen to!

I would highly recommend Dr. Hodge. I had him for PHYS 131 & 132 and he was great. VERY good at explaining tough concepts, which is imperative with this content. He is SUPER approachable during his office hours and truly wants you to learn. Tests are tough but fair and labs are guided well. He truly is a great teacher and encourage all to take him.

Great professor! Tests were definitely challenging so make sure you keep up with the material. Very helpful in office hours. Clear grading criteria and was always prepared for lecture. Definitely recommend.

Will is a 10/10 prof! His lectures were so engaging - he made a 3 hour class fly by. He's funny too!
Grade structure is also very fair: 3 exams which are hard but not impossible (worth 15% each and the final 20%), a quiz every week (10% total), lab 15% and hw 10%. If you're taking 131 take it with Will!! :)

One homework one quiz a week, three exams and a final. Exams are def harder than hw and quizzes. Really makes you understand the concepts well. This was a hard course but he made it fun and interactive. If you are willing to put in a lot of time, you can get a lot out of him and the course. He's very helpful inside and outside of class. Funny too

I loved Dr. Hodge and he may have even convinced me to be a physics minor. He is the best physics teacher at UR and is a great teacher. If you have the chance to take his class over another teacher, DO IT. PHYS 131 was the same as a highschool physics so nothing was new to me. Easy labs and the homework wasn't bad (once per week). 1 quiz per week.
Will's lectures actually made my day. He is very smart and enthusiastic about physics - funny too. He's the reason I finally understand the right hand rule! Would take again in a heartbeat.

PHYS131 is a typical lecture course, but Dr. Hodge makes the 2 hour lectures fly by with his fun teaching style. Plus, he is always willing to help when a topic is difficult, and he will make sure you can find the right answer. He is extremely accessible outside of class, and although his exams are relatively difficult, his class is enjoyable.

Dr. Hodge is the goat. Best physics professor at UR. He does lots of practice problems in class and is happy to answer any questions. The HW problems are a similar difficulty (if not more difficult) than the tests, which is great prep. The lab portion of the class is super easy and he's hilarious. Also a super fair grader.
